abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may draw cards until you have 3 cards in your hand.

attacks.name: Genome Hacking
attacks.text: Choose 1 of your opponent's Active Pokémon's attacks and use it as this attack.

d.name: Gardevoir ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Psychic Embrace
abilities.text: As often as you like during your turn, you may attach a Basic Psychic Energy card from your discard pile to 1 of your Psychic Pokémon. If you attached Energy to a Pokémon in this way, put 2 damage counters on that Pokémon. You can't use this Ability on a Pokémon that would be Knocked Out.

attacks.name: Miracle Force
attacks.text: This Pokémon recovers from all Special Conditions.

d.name: Charizard ex
rules: Tera: As long as this Pokémon is on your Bench, prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks (both yours and your opponent's).
Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Infernal Reign
abilities.text: When you play this Pokémon from your hand to evolve 1 of your Pokémon during your turn, you may search your deck for up to 3 Basic Fire Energy cards and attach them to your Pokémon in any way you like. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Burning Darkness
attacks.text: This attack does 30 more damage for each Prize card your opponent has taken.

d.name: Arven
rules: Search your deck for an Item card and a Pokémon Tool card, reveal them, and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

d.name: Clive
rules: Your opponent reveals their hand, and you draw 2 cards for each Supporter card you find there.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

d.name: Iono
rules: Each player shuffles their hand and puts it on the bottom of their deck. If either player put any cards on the bottom of their deck in this way, each player draws a card for each of their remaining Prize cards.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

d.name: Nemona
rules: Draw 3 cards.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

d.name: Penny
rules: Put 1 of your Basic Pokémon and all attached cards into your hand.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

d.name: Wo-Chien ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Covetous Ivy
attacks.text: This attack does 60 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon for each Prize card your opponent has taken. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

d.name: Chi-Yu ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Jealously Singe
attacks.text: Discard the top 2 cards of your opponent's deck.

attacks.name: Flame Surge
attacks.text: Choose up to 3 of your Benched Pokémon. For each of those Pokémon, search your deck for a Basic Fire Energy card and attach it to that Pokémon. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.name: Chien-Pao ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Shivery Chill
abilities.text: Once during your turn, if this Pokémon is in the Active Spot, you may search your deck for up to 2 Basic Water Energy cards, reveal them, and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Hail Blade
attacks.text: You may discard any amount of Water Energy from your Pokémon. This attack does 60 damage for each card you discarded in this way.

d.name: Miraidon ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Tandem Unit
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may search your deck for up to 2 Basic Lightning Pokémon and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Photon Blaster
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't attack.

d.name: Ting-Lu ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Cursed Land
abilities.text: As long as this Pokémon is in the Active Spot, your opponent's Pokémon in play that have any damage counters on them have no Abilities, except for Pokémon ex.

attacks.name: Land Scoop
attacks.text: Put 2 damage counters on 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon.

d.name: Koraidon ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Dino Cry
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may attach up to 2 Basic Fighting Energy cards from your discard pile to your Basic Fighting Pokémon in any way you like. If you use this Ability, your turn ends.

attacks.name: Wild Impact
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't attack.

d.name: Scyther

attacks.name: Slashing Strike
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't use Slashing Strike.

d.flavorText: The sharp scythes on its forearms become increasingly sharp by cutting through hard objects.

d.name: Pineco
d.flavorText: It spits out a fluid that it uses to glue tree bark to its body. The fluid hardens when it touches air.

d.name: Seedot

attacks.name: Rigidify
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 30 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

d.flavorText: If it remains still, it looks just like a real nut. It delights in surprising foraging Pokémon.

d.name: Nuzleaf

attacks.name: Comet Slap
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. This attack does 30 damage for each heads.

d.flavorText: It lives deep in forests. With the leaf on its head, it makes a flute whose song makes listeners uneasy.

d.name: Shiftry

attacks.name: Expelling Tornado
attacks.text: Choose 3 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. If you do, shuffle all of your opponent's Benched Pokémon that you didn't choose, and all cards attached to those Pokémon, into their deck.

attacks.name: Energy Loop
attacks.text: Put an Energy attached to this Pokémon into your hand.

d.flavorText: A Pokémon that was feared as a forest guardian. It can read the foe's mind and take preemptive action.

d.name: Shroomish

attacks.name: Double Headbutt
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 10 damage for each heads.

d.flavorText: If it senses danger, it scatters spores from the top of its head to protect itself.

d.name: Breloom

attacks.name: Knuckle Impact
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't attack.

d.flavorText: The seeds on its tail are made of toxic spores. It knocks out foes with quick, virtually invisible punches.

d.name: Roselia

abilities.name: Poison Point
abilities.text: If this Pokémon is in the Active Spot and is damaged by an attack from your opponent's Pokémon (even if this Pokémon is Knocked Out), the Attacking Pokémon is now Poisoned.

d.flavorText: Its flowers give off a relaxing fragrance. The stronger its aroma, the healthier the Roselia is.

d.name: Roserade

abilities.name: Poison Point
abilities.text: If this Pokémon is in the Active Spot and is damaged by an attack from your opponent's Pokémon (even if this Pokémon is Knocked Out), the Attacking Pokémon is now Poisoned.

attacks.name: Bind Down
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon can't retreat.

d.flavorText: After captivating opponents with its sweet scent, it lashes them with its thorny whips.

d.name: Turtwig

abilities.name: Solid Shell
abilities.text: This Pokémon takes 20 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

d.flavorText: Photosynthesis occurs across its body under the sun. The shell on its back is actually hardened soil.

d.name: Grotle

attacks.name: Ramming Shell
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 20 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

d.flavorText: It lives along water in forests. In the daytime, it leaves the forest to sunbathe its treed shell.

d.name: Torterra ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Forest March
attacks.text: This attack does 30 damage for each of your Grass Pokémon in play.

attacks.name: Jungle Hammer
attacks.text: Heal 50 damage from this Pokémon.

d.name: Shaymin

attacks.name: Pinpoint Dive
attacks.text: This attack does 60 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon ex or Benched Pokémon V. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

d.flavorText: It can dissolve toxins in the air to instantly transform ruined land into a lush field of flowers.

d.name: Cottonee

attacks.name: Triple Spin
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. This attack does 10 damage for each heads.

d.flavorText: It shoots cotton from its body to protect itself. If it gets caught up in hurricane-strength winds, it can get sent to the other side of the Earth.

d.name: Whimsicott

abilities.name: Wafting Heal
abilities.text: When you play this Pokémon from your hand to evolve 1 of your Pokémon during your turn, you may heal all damage from your Active Grass Pokémon. If you healed any damage in this way, discard all Energy from that Pokémon.

d.flavorText: It scatters cotton all over the place as a prank. If it gets wet, it'll become too heavy to move and have no choice but to answer for its mischief.

d.name: Deerling

attacks.name: Leaf Litter Tackle
attacks.text: Discard a Grass Energy from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Deerling have different scents depending on the season. In this form, Deerling have a softly sweet scent that lingers in the nose.

d.name: Sawsbuck

abilities.name: Changing Seasons
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may search your deck for a Stadium card, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: Sawsbuck in their Autumn Form are known for having very short tempers. The males fight each other incessantly.

d.name: Grubbin

attacks.name: Flock
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 Grubbin and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: Its natural enemies, like Rookidee, may flee rather than risk getting caught in its large mandibles that can snap thick tree branches.

d.name: Dhelmise

attacks.name: Steel Anchor
attacks.text: If you have any Metal Pokémon on your Bench, this attack does 80 more damage.

d.flavorText: After a piece of seaweed merged with debris from a sunken ship, it was reborn as this ghost Pokémon.

d.name: Bramblin
d.flavorText: Not even Bramblin knows where it is headed as it tumbles across the wilderness, blown by the wind. It loathes getting wet.

d.name: Brambleghast

abilities.name: Resilient Soul
abilities.text: This Pokémon gets +50 HP for each Prize card your opponent has taken.

attacks.name: Powerful Needles
attacks.text: Flip a coin for each Energy attached to this Pokémon. This attack does 80 damage for each heads.

d.flavorText: Brambleghast wanders around arid regions. On rare occasions, mass outbreaks of these Pokémon will bury an entire town.

d.name: Scovillain ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Chili Snapper Bind
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned. During your opponent's next turn, that Pokémon can't retreat.

attacks.name: Two-Headed Crushing
attacks.text: Discard a random card from your opponent's hand. Discard the top card of your opponent's deck.

d.name: Rellor

attacks.name: Slight Intrusion
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 10 damage to itself.

d.flavorText: It rolls its mud ball around while the energy it needs for evolution matures. Eventually the time comes for it to evolve.

d.name: Rabsca

abilities.name: Spherical Shield
abilities.text: Prevent all damage from and effects of attacks from your opponent's Pokémon done to your Benched Pokémon.

attacks.name: Psychic
attacks.text: This attack does 30 more damage for each Energy attached to your opponent's Active Pokémon.

d.flavorText: An infant sleeps inside the ball. Rabsca rolls the ball soothingly with its legs to ensure the infant sleeps comfortably.

d.name: Iron Leaves ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Rapid Vernier
abilities.text: When you play this Pokémon from your hand onto your Bench during your turn, you may switch it with your Active Pokémon. If you do, you may move any amount of Energy from your other Pokémon to this Pokémon.

attacks.name: Prism Edge
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't attack.

d.name: Ponyta

attacks.name: Charge Energy
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Basic Energy card, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: It can't run properly when it's newly born. As it races around with others of its kind, its legs grow stronger.

d.name: Rapidash

attacks.name: Inferno Onrush
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 30 damage to itself.

d.flavorText: This Pokémon can be seen galloping through fields at speeds of up to 150 mph, its fiery mane fluttering in the wind.

d.name: Slugma

attacks.name: Roasting Heat
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon is Burned, this attack does 40 more damage.

d.flavorText: A common sight in volcanic areas, it slowly slithers around in a constant search for warm places.

d.name: Magcargo

abilities.name: Lava Zone
abilities.text: Whenever your opponent's Active Pokémon moves to the Bench during their turn, their new Active Pokémon is now Burned.

d.flavorText: Its brittle shell occasionally spouts intense flames that circulate throughout its body.

d.name: Victini

attacks.name: Flippity Flap
attacks.text: Shuffle your hand into your deck. Then, draw 6 cards.

attacks.name: Singe Off
attacks.text: Discard a Special Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

d.flavorText: This Pokémon brings victory. It is said that Trainers with Victini always win, regardless of the type of encounter.

d.name: Heatmor

attacks.name: Licking Flames
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. For each tails, discard an Energy from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: There's a hole in its tail that allows it to draw in the air it needs to keep its fire burning. If the hole gets blocked, this Pokémon will fall ill.

d.name: Litten

attacks.name: Fake Out
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

d.flavorText: It spends even the smallest amount of downtime grooming its fur with its tongue. Loose fur gathers in its stomach and serves as fuel for fiery moves.

d.name: Torracat

attacks.name: Flare Strike
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't use Flare Strike.

d.flavorText: In the midst of battle, the fire pouch on Torracat's neck rings like a bell and produces stronger flames than usual.

d.name: Incineroar ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Hustle Play
abilities.text: Attacks used by this Pokémon cost Colorless less for each of your opponent's Benched Pokémon.

attacks.name: Blaze Blast
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned.

d.name: Turtonator

attacks.name: Spit-Out Shot
attacks.text: This attack does 40 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

d.flavorText: Explosive substances coat the shell on its back. Enemies that dare attack it will be blown away by an immense detonation.

d.name: Sizzlipede

attacks.name: Heat Dive
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 10 damage to itself.

d.flavorText: It stores flammable gas in its body and uses it to generate heat. The yellow sections on its belly get particularly hot.

d.name: Centiskorch

attacks.name: Singe
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned.

attacks.name: Charring Breath
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon isn't Burned, this attack does nothing.

d.flavorText: When it heats up, its body temperature reaches about 1,500 degrees Fahrenheit. It lashes its body like a whip and launches itself at enemies.

d.name: Gouging Fire ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Blaze Blitz
attacks.text: This Pokémon can't use Blaze Blitz again until it leaves the Active Spot.

d.name: Totodile

attacks.name: Big Bite
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon can't retreat.

d.flavorText: It is small but rough and tough. It won't hesitate to take a bite out of anything that moves.

d.name: Croconaw

attacks.name: Reverse Thrust
attacks.text: Switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

d.flavorText: If it loses a fang, a new one grows back in its place. There are always 48 fangs lining its mouth.

d.name: Feraligatr

abilities.name: Torrential Heart
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may put 5 damage counters on this Pokémon. If you do, during this turn, attacks used by this Pokémon do 120 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Giant Wave
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't use Giant Wave.

d.flavorText: It usually moves slowly, but it goes at blinding speed when it attacks and bites prey.

d.name: Carvanha
d.flavorText: It won't attack while it's alone—not even if it spots prey. Instead, it waits for other Carvanha to join it, and then the Pokémon attack as a group.

d.name: Sharpedo

attacks.name: Chew Off
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. For each heads, discard a random card from your opponent's hand.

d.flavorText: As soon as it catches the scent of prey, Sharpedo will jet seawater from its backside, hurtling toward the target to attack at 75 mph.

d.name: Keldeo

attacks.name: Rapid Draw
attacks.text: Draw 2 cards.

d.flavorText: Keldeo has strengthened its resolve for battle, filling its body with power and changing its form.

d.name: Snom

attacks.name: Powder Snow
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

d.flavorText: It eats snow that has accumulated on the ground. It prefers soft, freshly fallen snow, so it will eat its way up a mountain, aiming for the peak.

d.name: Frosmoth

attacks.name: Freezing Chill
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon can't attack.

d.flavorText: Frosmoth senses air currents with its antennae. It sends its scales drifting on frigid air, making them fall like snow.

d.name: Wiglett

attacks.name: Lucky Find
attacks.text: Search your deck for an Item card, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Aqua Bomb
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 20 damage to itself.

d.flavorText: This Pokémon can pick up the scent of a Veluza just over 65 feet away and will hide itself in the sand.

d.name: Finizen
d.flavorText: It likes playing with others of its kind using the water ring on its tail. It uses ultrasonic waves to sense the emotions of other living creatures.

d.name: Palafin

attacks.name: Vanguard Punch
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 10 damage to itself for each damage counter on it.

attacks.name: Double Hit
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 90 damage for each heads.

d.flavorText: This Pokémon's ancient genes have awakened. It is now so extraordinarily strong that it can easily lift a cruise ship with one fin.

d.name: Walking Wake ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Azure Seas
abilities.text: Damage from attacks used by this Pokémon isn't affected by any effects on your opponent's Active Pokémon.

attacks.name: Catharsis Roar
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon is affected by a Special Condition, this attack does 120 more damage.

d.name: Pikachu

attacks.name: Random Spark
attacks.text: This attack does 10 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

d.flavorText: When several of these Pokémon gather, their electricity can build and cause lightning storms.

d.name: Raichu

attacks.name: Collateral Bolts
attacks.text: This attack does 50 damage to each Pokémon that has any damage counters on it (both yours and your opponent's), except for this Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

d.flavorText: If the electric pouches in its cheeks become fully charged, both ears will stand straight up.

d.name: Electabuzz
d.flavorText: Many power plants keep Ground-type Pokémon around as a defense against Electabuzz that come seeking electricity.

d.name: Electivire

attacks.name: Short-Circuit Knuckle
attacks.text: If your opponent has any Water Pokémon in play, this attack does 120 more damage.

d.flavorText: The amount of electrical energy this Pokémon produces is proportional to the rate of its pulse. The voltage jumps while Electivire is battling.

d.name: Charjabug
d.flavorText: While its durable shell protects it from attacks, Charjabug strikes at enemies with jolts of electricity discharged from the tips of its jaws.

d.name: Vikavolt

attacks.name: Circuit Cannon
attacks.text: This attack does 80 more damage for each of your Benched Charjabug.

d.flavorText: It builds up electricity in its abdomen, focuses it through its jaws, and then fires the electricity off in concentrated beams.

d.name: Zeraora

attacks.name: Shocking Knuckle
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Strong Volt
attacks.text: Discard an Energy from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: It runs as fast as lightning strikes, shredding its opponents with its high-voltage claws.

d.name: Yamper

attacks.name: Whimsy Tackle
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

d.flavorText: This Pokémon is very popular as a herding dog in the Galar region. As it runs, it generates electricity from the base of its tail.

d.name: Boltund

attacks.name: Electrifying Dash
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 Basic Lightning Energy cards and attach them to your Benched Pokémon in any way you like. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: This Pokémon generates electricity and channels it into its legs to keep them going strong. Boltund can run nonstop for three full days.

d.name: Wugtrio ex
rules: As long as this Pokémon is on your Bench, prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks (both yours and your opponent's).
Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.
Tera: As long as this Pokémon is on your Bench, prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks (both yours and your opponent's).

attacks.name: Tricolor Pump
attacks.text: Discard up to 3 Energy cards from your hand. This attack does 60 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon for each Energy card you discarded in this way. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

attacks.name: Numbing Hold
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon can't retreat.

d.name: Iron Hands

attacks.name: Volt Wave
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Superalloy Hands
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon is a Pokémon ex or Pokémon V, this attack does 80 more damage.

d.flavorText: This Pokémon shares many similarities with Iron Hands, an object mentioned in a certain expedition journal.

d.name: Iron Thorns

attacks.name: Destructo-Press
attacks.text: Reveal the top 5 cards of your deck. This attack does 70 damage for each Future card you find there. Then, discard those Future cards and shuffle the other cards back into your deck.

d.flavorText: Some of its notable features match those of an object named within a certain expedition journal as Iron Thorns.

d.name: Mr. Mime

attacks.name: Look-Alike Show
attacks.text: Your opponent reveals their hand. You may use the effect of a Supporter card you find there as the effect of this attack.

attacks.name: Eerie Wave
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

d.flavorText: The broadness of its hands may be no coincidence—many scientists believe its palms became enlarged specifically for pantomiming.

d.name: Marill

attacks.name: Ball Roll
attacks.text: Flip a coin until you get tails. This attack does 10 damage for each heads.

d.flavorText: The fur on its body naturally repels water. It can stay dry even when it plays in the water.

d.name: Azumarill

attacks.name: Play Rough
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 30 more damage.

attacks.name: Power Tackle
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't attack.

d.flavorText: Its long ears are superb sensors. It can distinguish the movements of things in water and tell what they are.

d.name: Girafarig

attacks.name: Psychic Assault
attacks.text: This attack does 10 more damage for each damage counter on your opponent's Active Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Girafarig's tail has a small head. It instinctively bites at any foe that approaches the Pokémon from behind.

d.name: Latias

attacks.name: Allure
attacks.text: Draw 2 cards.

d.flavorText: It communicates using telepathy. Its body is covered in down that refracts light to make it invisible.

d.name: Bronzor

attacks.name: Mirror Attack
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon is a Psychic Pokémon, this attack does 30 more damage.

d.flavorText: Ancient people believed that the pattern on Bronzor's back contained a mysterious power.

d.name: Bronzong

attacks.name: Evolution Jammer
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, they can't play any Pokémon from their hand to evolve their Pokémon.

d.flavorText: In ages past, this Pokémon was revered as a bringer of rain. It was found buried in the ground.

d.name: Solosis

attacks.name: Surprise Attack
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

d.flavorText: It communicates with others telepathically. Its body is encapsulated in liquid, but if it takes a heavy blow, the liquid will leak out.

d.name: Duosion

attacks.name: Double Trick
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 30 damage for each heads.

d.flavorText: Its psychic power can supposedly cover a range of more than half a mile—but only if its two brains can agree with each other.

d.name: Reuniclus

attacks.name: Summoning Gate
attacks.text: Look at the top 8 cards of your deck. You may put any number of Pokémon you find there onto your Bench. Shuffle the other cards back into your deck.

attacks.name: Brain Shake
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

d.flavorText: While it could use its psychic abilities in battle, this Pokémon prefers to swing its powerful arms around to beat opponents into submission.

d.name: Elgyem

attacks.name: Hide
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, during your opponent's next turn, prevent all damage from and effects of attacks done to this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: If this Pokémon stands near a TV, strange scenery will appear on the screen. That scenery is said to be from its home.

d.name: Beheeyem

attacks.name: Cosmic Beatdown
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage for each of your Pokémon in play.

d.flavorText: Whenever a Beheeyem visits a farm, a Dubwool mysteriously disappears.

d.name: Cutiefly

attacks.name: Mini Drain
attacks.text: Heal 10 damage from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Nectar and pollen are its favorite fare. You can find Cutiefly hovering around Gossifleur, trying to get some of Gossifleur's pollen.

d.name: Ribombee

attacks.name: Plentiful Pollen
attacks.text: During your next turn, if the Defending Pokémon is Knocked Out, take 2 more Prize cards.

d.flavorText: It makes pollen puffs from pollen and nectar. The puffs' effects depend on the type of ingredients and how much of each one is used.

d.name: Scream Tail

attacks.name: Supportive Singing
attacks.text: Heal 100 damage from 1 of your Benched Ancient Pokémon.

d.flavorText: There has been only one reported sighting of this Pokémon. It resembles a mysterious creature depicted in an old expedition journal.

d.name: Flutter Mane

abilities.name: Midnight Fluttering
abilities.text: As long as this Pokémon is in the Active Spot, your opponent's Active Pokémon has no Abilities, except for Midnight Fluttering.

attacks.name: Hex Hurl
attacks.text: Put 2 damage counters on your opponent's Benched Pokémon in any way you like.

d.flavorText: This Pokémon has characteristics similar to those of Flutter Mane, a creature mentioned in a certain book.

d.name: Iron Valiant

attacks.name: Gemini Laser
attacks.text: This attack also does 20 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

attacks.name: Zen Blade
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't use Zen Blade.

d.flavorText: It's possible that this is the object listed as Iron Valiant in a certain expedition journal.

d.name: Iron Valiant

attacks.name: Calculation
attacks.text: Look at the top 4 cards of your deck and put them back in any order.

attacks.name: Majestic Sword
attacks.text: If you played a Future Supporter card from your hand during this turn, this attack does 100 more damage.

d.flavorText: It's possible that this is the object listed as Iron Valiant in a certain expedition journal.

d.name: Iron Crown ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Cobalt Command
abilities.text: Attacks used by your Future Pokémon, except any Iron Crown ex, do 20 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Twin Shotels
attacks.text: This attack does 50 damage to 2 of your opponent's Pokémon. This attack's damage isn't affected by Weakness or Resistance, or by any effects on those Pokémon.

d.name: Meditite
d.flavorText: It meditates to heighten its inner energy and to float in the air. It eats one berry a day.

d.name: Medicham
d.flavorText: It elegantly avoids attacks with dance-like steps, then launches a devastating blow in the same motion.

d.name: Relicanth

abilities.name: Memory Dive
abilities.text: Each of your evolved Pokémon can use any attack from its previous Evolutions. (You still need the necessary Energy to use each attack.)

d.flavorText: Rock-hard scales and oil-filled swim bladders allow this Pokémon to survive the intense water pressure of the deep sea.

d.name: Drilbur

abilities.name: Dig Dig Dig
abilities.text: When you play this Pokémon from your hand onto your Bench during your turn, you may search your deck for up to 3 Basic Fighting Energy cards and discard them. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: It brings its claws together and whirls around at high speed before rushing toward its prey.

d.name: Excadrill

attacks.name: Wild Tackle
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 50 damage to itself.

d.flavorText: It's not uncommon for tunnels that appear to have formed naturally to actually be a result of Excadrill's rampant digging.

d.name: Golett

attacks.name: Iron Defense
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, during your opponent's next turn, prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks.

d.flavorText: They were sculpted from clay in ancient times. No one knows why, but some of them are driven to continually line up boulders.

d.name: Golurk

attacks.name: Iron Defense
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, during your opponent's next turn, prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks.

attacks.name: Fighting Fist
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon is a Pokémon ex or Pokémon V, this attack does 120 more damage.

d.flavorText: Artillery platforms built into the walls of ancient castles served as perches from which Golurk could fire energy beams.

d.name: Rockruff
d.flavorText: This Pokémon is very friendly when it's young. Its disposition becomes vicious once it matures, but it never forgets the kindness of its master.

d.name: Lycanroc

attacks.name: Turbo Edge
attacks.text: Attach up to 2 Basic Fighting Energy cards from your discard pile to your Benched Pokémon in any way you like.

d.flavorText: Lycanroc attacks its prey with its sharp claws and fangs. It loyally obeys the instructions of a Trainer it trusts.

d.name: Mudbray
d.flavorText: This Pokémon covers itself in mud that it has regurgitated. The mud won't dry out even if it's exposed to the sun for a long time.

d.name: Mudsdale

attacks.name: Mud Stock
attacks.text: Attach a Basic Fighting Energy card from your discard pile to each of your Benched Pokémon.

attacks.name: High Horsepower
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 40 damage to itself.

d.flavorText: This Pokémon has been treasured not just for its physical labor but also because it produces high-quality mud used for making pottery.

d.name: Rolycoly
d.flavorText: On sunny days, Rolycoly will come out onto grassy plains and roll around. Then it will eat the grass that gets tangled in its wheel-like leg.

d.name: Carkol

attacks.name: Knock Away
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 40 more damage.

d.flavorText: The temperature inside its body increases when it experiences strong emotions. It rolls around frantically while spewing flames.

d.name: Coalossal

attacks.name: Gatling Tar
attacks.text: This attack does 80 more damage for each Fire Energy attached to this Pokémon.

attacks.name: Cragalanche
attacks.text: Discard the top 2 cards of your opponent's deck.

d.flavorText: To intimidate its opponents, Coalossal will vigorously shake its body, scattering coal from its smoldering back.

d.name: Great Tusk

attacks.name: Wrathful Charge
attacks.text: If your Benched Pokémon have any damage counters on them, this attack does 80 more damage.

d.flavorText: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. The name Great Tusk was taken from a creature listed in a certain book.

d.name: Great Tusk

attacks.name: Land Collapse
attacks.text: Discard the top card of your opponent's deck. If you played an Ancient Supporter card from your hand during this turn, discard 3 more cards in this way.

d.flavorText: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. The name Great Tusk was taken from a creature listed in a certain book.

d.name: Sandy Shocks

attacks.name: Magnetic Burst
attacks.text: If you have 3 or more Energy in play, this attack does 70 more damage. This attack's damage isn't affected by Weakness.

d.flavorText: No records exist of this Pokémon being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon's traits match up with a creature shown in an expedition journal.

d.name: Iron Boulder ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Repulsor Axe
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, if this Pokémon is damaged by an attack (even if it is Knocked Out), put 8 damage counters on the Attacking Pokémon.

attacks.name: Power Stomp
attacks.text: Discard 2 Energy from this Pokémon.

d.name: Ekans

attacks.name: Poison Blend
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused and Poisoned.

d.flavorText: The older it gets, the longer it grows. At night, it wraps its long body around tree branches to rest.

d.name: Arbok

attacks.name: Panic Poison
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned, Confused, and Poisoned.

d.flavorText: The pattern on its belly appears to be a frightening face. Weak foes will flee just at the sight of the pattern.

d.name: Gastly

attacks.name: Mysterious Beam
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, discard an Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

d.flavorText: It wraps its opponent in its gas-like body, slowly weakening its prey by poisoning it through the skin.

d.name: Haunter

attacks.name: Super Poison Breath
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Poisoned.

d.flavorText: It likes to lurk in the dark and tap shoulders with a gaseous hand. Its touch causes endless shuddering.

d.name: Gengar ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Gnawing Curse
abilities.text: Whenever your opponent attaches an Energy card from their hand to 1 of their Pokémon, put 2 damage counters on that Pokémon.

attacks.name: Tricky Steps
attacks.text: You may move an Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon to 1 of their Benched Pokémon.

d.name: Poochyena

attacks.name: Gnaw Off
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 20 more damage.

d.flavorText: A Pokémon with a persistent nature, it chases its chosen prey until the prey becomes exhausted.

d.name: Mightyena

attacks.name: Kick Away
attacks.text: Switch out your opponent's Active Pokémon to the Bench. (Your opponent chooses the new Active Pokémon.)

d.flavorText: It will always obey the commands of a skilled Trainer. Its behavior arises from its living in packs in ancient times.

d.name: Sableye

attacks.name: Damage Collection
attacks.text: You may move any number of damage counters from your opponent's Benched Pokémon to their Active Pokémon.

d.flavorText: It dwells in the darkness of caves. It uses its sharp claws to dig up gems to nourish itself.

d.name: Farigiraf ex
rules: As long as this Pokémon is on your Bench, prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks (both yours and your opponent's).
Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.
Tera: As long as this Pokémon is on your Bench, prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks (both yours and your opponent's).

abilities.name: Armor Tail
abilities.text: Prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks from your opponent's Basic Pokémon ex.

attacks.name: Dirty Beam
attacks.text: This attack also does 30 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

d.name: Roaring Moon

attacks.name: Vengeance Fletching
attacks.text: This attack does 10 more damage for each Ancient card in your discard pile.

d.flavorText: It is possible that this is the creature listed as Roaring Moon in an expedition journal that still holds many mysteries.

d.name: Forretress

attacks.name: Spike Cannon
attacks.text: Flip 3 coins. This attack does 30 damage for each heads.

attacks.name: Steel Tackle
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 40 damage to itself.

d.flavorText: Its entire body is shielded by a steel-hard shell. What lurks inside this shell is a total mystery.

d.name: Scizor ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Steel Wing
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 50 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Cross Breaker
attacks.text: Discard up to 2 Metal Energy from this Pokémon. This attack does 120 damage for each card you discarded in this way.

d.name: Mawile

attacks.name: Invite and Strike
attacks.text: Switch in 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon to the Active Spot. This attack does 30 damage to the new Active Pokémon.

d.flavorText: It uses its docile-looking face to lull foes into complacency, then bites with its huge, relentless jaws.

d.name: Beldum

attacks.name: Iron Tackle
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 10 damage to itself.

d.flavorText: From its rear, Beldum emits a magnetic force that rapidly pulls opponents in. They get skewered on Beldum's sharp claws.

d.name: Metang

abilities.name: Metal Maker
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may look at the top 4 cards of your deck and attach any number of Basic Metal Energy cards you find there to your Pokémon in any way you like. Shuffle the other cards and put them on the bottom of your deck.

d.flavorText: Two Beldum have become stuck together via their own magnetic forces. With two brains, the resulting Metang has doubled psychic powers.

d.name: Metagross

attacks.name: Meteor Mash
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon's Meteor Mash attack does 60 more damage (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Luster Blast
attacks.text: Discard 2 Energy from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Because the magnetic powers of these Pokémon get stronger in freezing temperatures, Metagross living on snowy mountains are full of energy.

d.name: Meltan
d.flavorText: It dissolves and eats metal. Circulating liquid metal within its body is how it generates energy.

d.name: Melmetal
d.flavorText: At the end of its life-span, Melmetal will rust and fall apart. The small shards left behind will eventually be reborn as Meltan.

d.name: Iron Treads

abilities.name: Dual Core
abilities.text: As long as this Pokémon has a Future Booster Energy Capsule attached, it is Fighting and Metal type.

attacks.name: Wheel Pass
attacks.text: Move an Energy from this Pokémon to 1 of your Benched Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. It resembles a mysterious object described in an old expedition journal.

d.name: Koraidon

attacks.name: Primordial Beatdown
attacks.text: This attack does 30 damage for each of your Ancient Pokémon in play.

attacks.name: Shred
attacks.text: This attack's damage isn't affected by any effects on your opponent's Active Pokémon.

d.flavorText: This seems to be the Winged King mentioned in an old expedition journal. It was said to have split the land with its bare fists.

d.name: Koraidon ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Retribution Strike
attacks.text: This attack does 10 more damage for each damage counter on this Pokémon.

attacks.name: Kaiser Tackle
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 60 damage to itself.

d.name: Miraidon

attacks.name: Peak Acceleration
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 Basic Energy cards and attach them to your Future Pokémon in any way you like. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: This seems to be the Iron Serpent mentioned in an old book. The Iron Serpent is said to have turned the land to ash with its lightning.

d.name: Miraidon ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Repulsion Bolt
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon already has any damage counters on it, this attack does 100 more damage.

attacks.name: Cyber Drive
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't use Cyber Drive.

d.name: Raging Bolt ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Burst Roar
attacks.text: Discard your hand and draw 6 cards.

attacks.name: Bellowing Thunder
attacks.text: You may discard any amount of Basic Energy from your Pokémon. This attack does 70 damage for each card you discarded in this way.

d.name: Lickitung

attacks.name: Tongue Pull
attacks.text: Your opponent reveals their hand. Put up to 2 Basic Pokémon you find there onto your opponent's Bench.

d.flavorText: If this Pokémon's sticky saliva gets on you and you don't clean it off, an intense itch will set in. The itch won't go away, either.

d.name: Lickilicky

attacks.name: Body Slam
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

attacks.name: Tonguenado
attacks.text: Flip 4 coins. This attack does 70 damage for each heads.

d.flavorText: Lickilicky's strange tongue can stretch to many times the length of its body. No one has figured out how Lickilicky's tongue can stretch so far.

d.name: Hoothoot

attacks.name: Silent Wing
attacks.text: Your opponent reveals their hand.

d.flavorText: It always stands on one foot. It changes feet so fast, the movement can rarely be seen.

d.name: Noctowl

attacks.name: Talon Hunt
attacks.text: You may search your deck for up to 2 cards and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: Its eyes are specially developed to enable it to see clearly even in murky darkness and minimal light.

d.name: Dunsparce

attacks.name: Dig
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, during your opponent's next turn, prevent all damage from and effects of attacks done to this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: It creates mazes in dark locations. When spotted, it flees into the ground by digging with its tail.

d.name: Dudunsparce

abilities.name: Run Away Draw
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may draw 3 cards. If you drew any cards in this way, shuffle this Pokémon and all attached cards into your deck.

d.flavorText: This Pokémon uses its hard tail to make its nest by boring holes into bedrock deep underground. The nest can reach lengths of over six miles.

d.name: Skitty

attacks.name: Call for Family
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Basic Pokémon and put it onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: It can't stop itself from chasing moving things, and it runs in a circle, chasing its own tail.

d.name: Delcatty

attacks.name: Tail Trickery
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

attacks.name: Energy Blender
attacks.text: You may move any amount of Energy from your Pokémon to your other Pokémon in any way you like.

d.flavorText: It dislikes dirty places. It often searches for a comfortable place in which to groom itself.

d.name: Chatot

attacks.name: A Cappella
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 3 Basic Pokémon and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: It mimics the cries of other Pokémon to trick them into thinking it's one of them. This way they won't attack it.

d.name: Pidove

abilities.name: Emergency Evolution
abilities.text: Once during your turn, if this Pokémon's remaining HP is 30 or less, you may search your deck for an Unfezant or Unfezant ex and put it onto this Pidove to evolve it. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: Where people go, these Pokémon follow. If you're scattering food for them, be careful— several hundred of them can gather at once.

d.name: Tranquill

attacks.name: Jet Wing
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't attack.

d.flavorText: It can fly moderately quickly. No matter how far it travels, it can always find its way back to its master and its nest.

d.name: Unfezant

attacks.name: Opposing Winds
attacks.text: You may put 2 Energy attached to your opponent's Active Pokémon into their hand.

attacks.name: Boundless Power
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't attack.

d.flavorText: Unfezant are exceptional fliers. The females are known for their stamina, while the males outclass them in terms of speed.

d.name: Minccino

attacks.name: Cleaning Up
attacks.text: Discard up to 2 Pokémon Tools from your opponent's Pokémon.

d.flavorText: The way it brushes away grime with its tail can be helpful when cleaning. But its focus on spotlessness can make cleaning more of a hassle.

d.name: Cinccino

attacks.name: Special Roll
attacks.text: This attack does 70 damage for each Special Energy card attached to this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Its body secretes oil that this Pokémon spreads over its nest as a coating to protect it from dust. Cinccino won't tolerate even a speck of the stuff.

d.name: Drampa

attacks.name: Raging Cannon
attacks.text: If all of your Benched Pokémon have at least 1 damage counter on them, this attack does 120 more damage.

d.flavorText: The mountains it calls home are nearly two miles in height. On rare occasions, it descends to play with the children living in the towns below.

d.name: Iron Jugulis

abilities.name: Automated Combat
abilities.text: If this Pokémon is in the Active Spot and is damaged by an attack from your opponent's Pokémon (even if this Pokémon is Knocked Out), put 3 damage counters on the Attacking Pokémon.

d.flavorText: It's possible that Iron Jugulis, an object described in an old book, may actually be this Pokémon.

d.name: Ancient Booster Energy Capsule
rules: The Ancient Pokémon this card is attached to gets +60 HP, recovers from all Special Conditions, and can't be affected by any Special Conditions.
You may attach any number of Pokémon Tools to your Pokémon during your turn. You may attach only 1 Pokémon Tool to each Pokémon, and it stays attached.

d.name: Awakening Drum
rules: Draw a card for each of your Ancient Pokémon in play.
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.
ACE SPEC: You can't have more than 1 ACE SPEC card in your deck.

d.name: Bianca's Devotion
rules: Heal all damage from 1 of your Pokémon that has 30 HP or less remaining.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

d.name: Boxed Order
rules: Search your deck for up to 2 Item cards, reveal them, and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck. Your turn ends.
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.

d.name: Buddy-Buddy Poffin
rules: Search your deck for up to 2 Basic Pokémon with 70 HP or less and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.

d.name: Ciphermaniac's Codebreaking
rules: Search your deck for 2 cards, shuffle your deck, then put those cards on top of it in any order.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

d.name: Eri
rules: Your opponent reveals their hand, and you discard up to 2 Item cards you find there.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

d.name: Explorer's Guidance
rules: Look at the top 6 cards of your deck and put 2 of them into your hand. Discard the other cards.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

d.name: Full Metal Lab
rules: Metal Pokémon (both yours and your opponent's) take 30 less damage from attacks from the opponent's Pokémon (after applying Weakness and Resistance).
You may play only 1 Stadium card during your turn. Put it into the Active Spot, and discard it if another Stadium comes into play. A Stadium with the same name can't be played.

d.name: Future Booster Energy Capsule
rules: The Future Pokémon this card is attached to has no Retreat Cost, and the attacks it uses do 20 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon (before applying Weakness and Resistance).
You may attach any number of Pokémon Tools to your Pokémon during your turn. You may attach only 1 Pokémon Tool to each Pokémon, and it stays attached.

d.name: Hand Trimmer
rules: Each player discards cards from their hand until they have 5 cards in their hand. Your opponent discards first. (If a player has 5 or fewer cards in their hand, they do not discard.)
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.

d.name: Heavy Baton
rules: If the Pokémon this card is attached to has a Retreat Cost of exactly 4, is in the Active Spot, and is Knocked Out by damage from an attack from your opponent's Pokémon, move up to 3 Basic Energy cards from that Pokémon to your Benched Pokémon in any way you like.
You may attach any number of Pokémon Tools to your Pokémon during your turn. You may attach only 1 Pokémon Tool to each Pokémon, and it stays attached.

d.name: Hero's Cape
rules: The Pokémon this card is attached to gets +100 HP.
You may attach any number of Pokémon Tools to your Pokémon during your turn. You may attach only 1 Pokémon Tool to each Pokémon, and it stays attached.
ACE SPEC: You can't have more than 1 ACE SPEC card in your deck.

d.name: Master Ball
rules: Search your deck for a Pokémon, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.
ACE SPEC: You can't have more than 1 ACE SPEC card in your deck.

d.name: Maximum Belt
rules: Attacks used by the Pokémon this card is attached to do 50 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon ex (before applying Weakness and Resistance).
You may attach any number of Pokémon Tools to your Pokémon during your turn. You may attach only 1 Pokémon Tool to each Pokémon, and it stays attached.
ACE SPEC: You can't have more than 1 ACE SPEC card in your deck.

d.name: Morty's Conviction
rules: You can use this card only if you discard another card from your hand.  Draw a card for each of your opponent's Benched Pokémon.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

d.name: Perilous Jungle
rules: During Pokémon Checkup, put 2 more damage counters on each Poisoned non-Darkness Pokémon (both yours and your opponent's).
You may play only 1 Stadium card during your turn. Put it next to the Active Spot, and discard it if another Stadium comes into play. A Stadium with the same name can't be played.
You may play only 1 Stadium card during your turn. Put it into the Active Spot, and discard it if another Stadium comes into play. A Stadium with the same name can't be played.

d.name: Prime Catcher
rules: Switch in 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon to the Active Spot. If you do, switch your Active Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon.
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.
ACE SPEC: You can't have more than 1 ACE SPEC card in your deck.

d.name: Reboot Pod
rules: Attach a Basic Energy card from your discard pile to each of your Future Pokémon.
You may play any number of Item cards during your turn.
ACE SPEC: You can't have more than 1 ACE SPEC card in your deck.

d.name: Rescue Board
rules: The Retreat Cost of the Pokémon this card is attached to is Colorless less. If that Pokémon's remaining HP is 30 or less, it has no Retreat Cost.
You may attach any number of Pokémon Tools to your Pokémon during your turn. You may attach only 1 Pokémon Tool to each Pokémon, and it stays attached.

d.name: Salvatore
rules: Search your deck for a card that has no Abilities and evolves from 1 of your Pokémon, and put it onto that Pokémon to evolve it. Then, shuffle your deck. You can use this card on a Pokémon you put down when you were setting up to play or on a Pokémon that was put into play this turn.
You may play only 1 Supporter card during your turn.

d.name: Mist Energy
rules: As long as this card is attached to a Pokémon, it provides Colorless Energy.    Prevent all effects of attacks used by your opponent's Pokémon done to the Pokémon this card is attached to. (Existing effects are not removed. Damage is not an effect.)

d.name: Neo Upper Energy
rules: You can't have more than 1 ACE SPEC card in your deck.

As long as this card is attached to a Pokémon, it provides Colorless Energy.  If this card is attached to a Stage 2 Pokémon, this card provides every type of Energy but provides only 2 Energy at a time.
ACE SPEC: You can't have more than 1 ACE SPEC card in your deck.

d.name: Shiftry

attacks.name: Expelling Tornado
attacks.text: Choose 3 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon. If you do, shuffle all of your opponent's Benched Pokémon that you didn't choose, and all cards attached to those Pokémon, into their deck.

attacks.name: Energy Loop
attacks.text: Put an Energy attached to this Pokémon into your hand.

d.flavorText: A Pokémon that was feared as a forest guardian. It can read the foe's mind and take preemptive action.

d.name: Grotle

attacks.name: Ramming Shell
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 20 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

d.flavorText: It lives along water in forests. In the daytime, it leaves the forest to sunbathe its treed shell.

d.name: Deerling

attacks.name: Leaf Litter Tackle
attacks.text: Discard a Grass Energy from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Deerling have different scents depending on the season. In this form, Deerling have a softly sweet scent that lingers in the nose.

d.name: Sawsbuck

abilities.name: Changing Seasons
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may search your deck for a Stadium card, reveal it, and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: Sawsbuck in their Autumn Form are known for having very short tempers. The males fight each other incessantly.

d.name: Litten

attacks.name: Fake Out
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

d.flavorText: It spends even the smallest amount of downtime grooming its fur with its tongue. Loose fur gathers in its stomach and serves as fuel for fiery moves.

d.name: Snom

attacks.name: Powder Snow
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

d.flavorText: It eats snow that has accumulated on the ground. It prefers soft, freshly fallen snow, so it will eat its way up a mountain, aiming for the peak.

d.name: Charjabug
d.flavorText: While its durable shell protects it from attacks, Charjabug strikes at enemies with jolts of electricity discharged from the tips of its jaws.

d.name: Bronzor

attacks.name: Mirror Attack
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon is a Psychic Pokémon, this attack does 30 more damage.

d.flavorText: Ancient people believed that the pattern on Bronzor's back contained a mysterious power.

d.name: Reuniclus

attacks.name: Summoning Gate
attacks.text: Look at the top 8 cards of your deck. You may put any number of Pokémon you find there onto your Bench. Shuffle the other cards back into your deck.

attacks.name: Brain Shake
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Confused.

d.flavorText: While it could use its psychic abilities in battle, this Pokémon prefers to swing its powerful arms around to beat opponents into submission.

d.name: Cutiefly

attacks.name: Mini Drain
attacks.text: Heal 10 damage from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Nectar and pollen are its favorite fare. You can find Cutiefly hovering around Gossifleur, trying to get some of Gossifleur's pollen.

d.name: Relicanth

abilities.name: Memory Dive
abilities.text: Each of your evolved Pokémon can use any attack from its previous Evolutions. (You still need the necessary Energy to use each attack.)

d.flavorText: Rock-hard scales and oil-filled swim bladders allow this Pokémon to survive the intense water pressure of the deep sea.

d.name: Excadrill

attacks.name: Wild Tackle
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 50 damage to itself.

d.flavorText: It's not uncommon for tunnels that appear to have formed naturally to actually be a result of Excadrill's rampant digging.

d.name: Mudsdale

attacks.name: Mud Stock
attacks.text: Attach a Basic Fighting Energy card from your discard pile to each of your Benched Pokémon.

attacks.name: High Horsepower
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 40 damage to itself.

d.flavorText: This Pokémon has been treasured not just for its physical labor but also because it produces high-quality mud used for making pottery.

d.name: Arbok

attacks.name: Panic Poison
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned, Confused, and Poisoned.

d.flavorText: The pattern on its belly appears to be a frightening face. Weak foes will flee just at the sight of the pattern.

d.name: Gastly

attacks.name: Mysterious Beam
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, discard an Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

d.flavorText: It wraps its opponent in its gas-like body, slowly weakening its prey by poisoning it through the skin.

attacks.text: Discard up to 3 Energy cards from your hand. This attack does 60 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon for each Energy card you discarded in this way. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

attacks.name: Numbing Hold
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon can't retreat.

abilities.name: Cobalt Command

attacks.name: Twin Shotels

d.name: Tangela
d.flavorText: Hidden beneath a tangle of vines that grows nonstop even if the vines are torn off, this Pokémon's true appearance remains a mystery.

d.name: Tangrowth

abilities.name: Thicket Body
abilities.text: This Pokémon takes 30 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Loom Over
attacks.text: This attack does 10 less damage for each damage counter on this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Tangrowth has two arms that it can extend as it pleases. Recent research has shown that these arms are, in fact, bundles of vines.

d.name: Pinsir

attacks.name: Slow Crunch
attacks.text: Discard all Energy from this Pokémon. At the end of your opponent's next turn, the Defending Pokémon will be Knocked Out.

d.flavorText: These Pokémon judge one another based on pincers. Thicker, more impressive pincers make for more popularity with the opposite gender.

d.name: Spinarak
d.flavorText: Some fishers weave its sturdy thread into nets to catch fish Pokémon.

d.name: Ariados

abilities.name: Big Net
abilities.text: Your opponent's Active Evolution Pokémon's Retreat Cost is Colorless more.

attacks.name: String Bind
attacks.text: This attack does 30 more damage for each Colorless in your opponent's Active Pokémon's Retreat Cost.

d.flavorText: It wanders in search of food after darkness falls, never nesting in a specific place.

d.name: Sunkern

attacks.name: Bullet Seed
attacks.text: Flip 4 coins. This attack does 10 damage for each heads.

d.flavorText: It is very weak. Its only means of defense is to shake its leaves desperately at its attacker.

d.name: Sunflora

attacks.name: Redirected Sunlight
attacks.text: This attack does 60 damage for each Fire Energy attached to all of your opponent's Pokémon.

attacks.name: Mega Drain
attacks.text: Heal 30 damage from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Since it converts sunlight into energy, it is always looking in the direction of the sun.

d.name: Heracross

attacks.name: Body Slam
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

d.flavorText: With its herculean powers, it can easily throw around an object that is 100 times its own weight.

d.name: Volbeat

attacks.name: Quick Sign
attacks.text: If you go first, you can use this attack during your first turn. Search your deck for up to 2 Basic Pokémon and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Coordinated Strike
attacks.text: If Illumise is on your Bench, this attack does 60 more damage.

d.flavorText: It flashes the light on its rear to communicate with other Volbeat. It loves the sweet aroma given off by Illumise.

d.name: Illumise

attacks.name: Slowing Perfume
attacks.text: You can use this attack only if you go second, and only during your first turn. Shuffle 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon and all attached cards into their deck.

d.flavorText: It guides Volbeat to draw signs in the night sky. There are scholars who research the meaning of these signs.

d.name: Leafeon

attacks.name: Leaflet Blessings
attacks.text: Attach a Basic Grass Energy card from your hand to 1 of your Benched Pokémon. If you do, heal all damage from that Pokémon.

d.flavorText: The younger they are, the more they smell like fresh grass. With age, their fragrance takes on the odor of fallen leaves.

d.name: Phantump

attacks.name: Leech Seed
attacks.text: Heal 20 damage from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: This Pokémon came to be when the spirit of a deceased child possessed a tree stump. It now wanders the forest searching for friends.

d.name: Trevenant

attacks.name: Giga Drain
attacks.text: Heal from this Pokémon the same amount of damage you did to your opponent's Active Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Trevenant is very kind to Pokémon living in the forest. It doesn't even care if these Pokémon take up residence in the greenery on its head.

d.name: Grookey
d.flavorText: When it uses its special stick to strike up a beat, the sound waves produced carry revitalizing energy to the plants and flowers in the area.

d.name: Thwackey

abilities.name: Boom Boom Groove
abilities.text: Once during your turn, if your Active Pokémon has the Festival Lead Ability, you may search your deck for a card and put it into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: The faster a Thwackey can beat out a rhythm with its two sticks, the more respect it wins from its peers.

d.name: Rillaboom

attacks.name: Drum Beating
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, attacks used by the Defending Pokémon cost Colorless more, and its Retreat Cost is Colorless more.

attacks.name: Wood Hammer
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 50 damage to itself.

d.flavorText: By drumming, it taps into the power of its special tree stump. The roots of the stump follow its direction in battle.

d.name: Applin

attacks.name: Tumbling Attack
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 20 more damage.

d.flavorText: Applin lives inside an apple. When an Applin is separated from its apple, its body loses moisture and the Pokémon grows weak.

d.name: Dipplin

abilities.name: Festival Lead
abilities.text: If Festival Grounds is in play, this Pokémon may use an attack it has twice. If the first attack Knocks Out your opponent's Active Pokémon, you may attack again after your opponent chooses a new Active Pokémon.

attacks.name: Do the Wave
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage for each of your Benched Pokémon.

d.flavorText: The head sticking out belongs to the fore-wyrm, while the tail belongs to the core-wyrm. The two share one apple and help each other out.

d.name: Iron Leaves

attacks.name: Recovery Net
attacks.text: Put up to 2 Pokémon from your discard pile into your hand.

attacks.name: Avenging Edge
attacks.text: If any of your Pokémon were Knocked Out by damage from an attack during your opponent's last turn, this attack does 60 more damage.

d.flavorText: According to the few eyewitness accounts that exist, it used its shining blades to julienne large trees and boulders.

d.name: Poltchageist

abilities.name: Storehouse Hideaway
abilities.text: As long as this Pokémon is on your Bench, prevent all damage from and effects of attacks from your opponent's Pokémon done to this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Poltchageist looks like a regional form of Sinistea, but it was recently discovered that the two Pokémon are entirely unrelated.

d.name: Poltchageist

attacks.name: Tea Server

attacks.name: Surprise Attack
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If tails, this attack does nothing.

d.flavorText: Poltchageist looks like a regional form of Sinistea, but it was recently discovered that the two Pokémon are entirely unrelated.

d.name: Sinistcha

attacks.name: Cursed Drop
attacks.text: Put 4 damage counters on your opponent's Pokémon in any way you like.

attacks.name: Spill the Tea
attacks.text: Discard up to 3 Grass Energy cards from your Pokémon. This attack does 70 damage for each card you discarded in this way.

d.flavorText: It prefers cool, dark places, such as the back of a shelf or the space beneath a home's floorboards. It wanders in search of prey after sunset.

rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.name: Matcha Splash

d.name: Teal Mask Ogerpon

attacks.name: Mountain Stroll
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 Basic Energy cards, reveal them, and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

attacks.name: Ogre Comeback
attacks.text: This attack does 20 more damage for each of your opponent's Benched Pokémon.

d.flavorText: This mischief-loving Pokémon is full of curiosity. It battles by drawing out the type-based energy contained within its masks.

abilities.name: Teal Dance
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may attach a Basic Grass Energy card from your hand to this Pokémon. If you attached Energy to a Pokémon in this way, draw a card.

attacks.name: Myriad Leaf Shower
attacks.text: This attack does 30 more damage for each Energy attached to both Active Pokémon.

d.name: Vulpix
d.flavorText: As its body grows larger, its six warm tails become more beautiful, with a more luxurious coat of fur.

d.name: Ninetales

attacks.name: Eerie Glow
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned and Confused.

d.flavorText: It has nine long tails and fur that gleams gold. It is said to live for 1,000 years.

d.name: Slugma

attacks.name: Hot Magma
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned.

d.flavorText: It's said that in ancient times, when volcanoes were more active, there were many more Slugma than there are now.

d.name: Magcargo ex
rules: As long as this Pokémon is on your Bench, prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks (both yours and your opponent's).

attacks.name: Hot Magma
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned.

attacks.name: Ground Burn
attacks.text: Discard the top card of each player's deck. This attack does 140 more damage for each Energy card discarded in this way.

d.name: Torkoal

attacks.name: Ramming Shell
attacks.text: During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes 30 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

attacks.name: Fire Spin
attacks.text: Discard 2 Energy from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Coal is the source of Torkoal's energy. Large amounts of coal can be found in the mountains where they live.

d.name: Chimchar

attacks.name: Firebreathing
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 20 more damage.

d.flavorText: Its fiery rear end is fueled by gas made in its belly. Even rain can't extinguish the fire.

d.name: Monferno

attacks.name: Heat Blow
attacks.text: Discard an Energy from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: It skillfully controls the intensity of the fire on its tail to keep its foes at an ideal distance.

d.name: Infernape

abilities.name: Pyro Dance
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may attach a Basic Fire Energy card, a Basic Fighting Energy card, or 1 of each from your hand to your Pokémon in any way you like.

attacks.name: Scorching Fire
attacks.text: Discard an Energy from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Its crown of fire is indicative of its fiery nature. It is beaten by none in terms of quickness.

d.name: Darumaka

attacks.name: Fire Tackle
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 20 damage to itself.

d.flavorText: It derives its power from fire burning inside its body. If the fire dwindles, this Pokémon will immediately fall asleep.

d.name: Darmanitan

attacks.name: Inferno Onrush
attacks.text: This Pokémon also does 70 damage to itself.

d.flavorText: The thick arms of this hot-blooded Pokémon can deliver punches capable of obliterating a dump truck.

d.name: Litwick

attacks.name: Call for Family
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Basic Pokémon and put it onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: While shining a light and pretending to be a guide, it leeches off the life-force of any who follow it.

d.name: Lampent

attacks.name: Burn It All Up
attacks.text: Discard all Energy from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: The spirits it absorbs fuel its baleful fire. It hangs around hospitals waiting for people to pass on.

d.name: Chandelure

abilities.name: Alluring Light
abilities.text: Once during your turn, you may have each player draw a card.

attacks.name: Mind Ruler
attacks.text: This attack does 30 damage for each card in your opponent's hand.

d.flavorText: It absorbs spirits, which it then burns. By waving the flames on its arms, it puts its foes into a hypnotic trance.

d.name: Chi-Yu

attacks.name: Allure
attacks.text: Draw 2 cards.

attacks.name: Ground Melter
attacks.text: If a Stadium is in play, this attack does 60 more damage. Then, discard that Stadium.

d.flavorText: The envy accumulated within curved beads that sparked multiple conflicts has clad itself in fire and become a Pokémon.

d.name: Hearthflame Mask Ogerpon ex
rules: As long as this Pokémon is on your Bench, prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks (both yours and your opponent's).
Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage for each damage counter on this Pokémon.

attacks.name: Dynamic Blaze
attacks.text: If your opponent's Active Pokémon is an Evolution Pokémon, this attack does 140 more damage, and discard all Energy from this Pokémon.

d.name: Poliwag

attacks.name: Tail Rap
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 20 damage for each heads.

d.flavorText: Its legs are newly grown, and it can't walk very well. It seems to prefer swimming through the water instead.

d.name: Poliwhirl

attacks.name: Hypnosis
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

attacks.name: Double Slap
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. This attack does 30 damage for each heads.

d.flavorText: Its skin is moist all over its body. The skin on its belly spiral also feels smooth.

d.name: Poliwrath

attacks.name: Hypnosis
attacks.text: Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Asleep.

attacks.name: Jumping Uppercut
attacks.text: You may do 120 more damage. If you do, shuffle this Pokémon and all attached cards into your deck.

d.flavorText: It can use its well-developed arms and legs to run on the surface of the water for a split second.

d.name: Goldeen

abilities.name: Festival Lead
abilities.text: If Festival Grounds is in play, this Pokémon may use an attack it has twice. If the first attack Knocks Out your opponent's Active Pokémon, you may attack again after your opponent chooses a new Active Pokémon.

attacks.name: Whirlpool
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, discard an Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

d.flavorText: Its dorsal, pectoral, and tail fins wave elegantly in water. That is why it is known as the Water Dancer.

d.name: Seaking

attacks.name: Peck Off
attacks.text: Before doing damage, discard all Pokémon Tools from your opponent's Active Pokémon.

d.flavorText: In autumn, its body becomes more fatty in preparing to propose to a mate. It takes on beautiful colors.

d.name: Jynx

attacks.name: Inviting Kiss
attacks.text: Search your deck for a Basic Pokémon and put it onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck. If you put any Pokémon onto your Bench in this way, move an Energy from this Pokémon to the new Benched Pokémon.

d.flavorText: In certain parts of Galar, Jynx was once feared and worshiped as the Queen of Ice.

d.name: Corphish
d.flavorText: It can live in impure water, where it doesn't need to compete with other water Pokémon for food, so its numbers have steadily increased.

d.name: Crawdaunt

attacks.name: Snip Snip
attacks.text: Flip 2 coins. For each heads, discard the top card of your opponent's deck.

attacks.name: Rampaging Hammer
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't attack.

d.flavorText: A rough customer that wildly flails its giant claws. It is said to be extremely hard to raise.

d.name: Feebas

attacks.name: Flail
attacks.text: This attack does 10 damage for each damage counter on this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: It is the shabbiest Pokémon of all. It forms schools and lives at the bottom of rivers that teem with plant life.

d.name: Milotic

abilities.name: Mentally Calm
abilities.text: Your opponent's Pokémon in play and all attached cards can't be put into your opponent's hand.

d.flavorText: It lives at the bottom of clear lakes. In times of war, it shows itself, which soothes people's minds and hearts.

d.name: Snorunt

attacks.name: Astonish
attacks.text: Choose a random card from your opponent's hand. Your opponent reveals that card and shuffles it into their deck.

d.flavorText: It is said that a home visited by a Snorunt will prosper. It can withstand cold of −150 degrees Fahrenheit.

d.name: Glalie

attacks.name: Damage Beat
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage for each damage counter on your opponent's Active Pokémon.

attacks.name: Crazy Headbutt
attacks.text: Discard an Energy from this Pokémon.

d.flavorText: It prevents prey from escaping by instantaneously freezing moisture in the air.

d.name: Froslass

abilities.name: Freezing Shroud
abilities.text: During Pokémon Checkup, put 1 damage counter on each Pokémon that has an Ability (both yours and your opponent's), except any Froslass.

d.flavorText: It freezes prey by blowing its −58 degree Fahrenheit breath. It is said to then secretly display its prey.

d.name: Glaceon

attacks.name: Permeating Chill
attacks.text: At the end of your opponent's next turn, put 9 damage counters on the Defending Pokémon.

d.flavorText: It lowers its body heat to freeze its fur. The hairs then become like needles it can fire.

d.name: Phione

attacks.name: Beckon
attacks.text: Put a Supporter card from your discard pile into your hand.

attacks.name: Energy Press
attacks.text: This attack does 20 damage for each Energy attached to your opponent's Active Pokémon.

d.flavorText: When the water warms, they inflate the flotation sac on their heads and drift languidly on the sea in packs.

d.name: Froakie

attacks.name: Flock
attacks.text: Search your deck for up to 2 Froakie and put them onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: It secretes flexible bubbles from its chest and back. The bubbles reduce the damage it would otherwise take when attacked.

d.name: Frogadier

attacks.name: Numbing Water
attacks.text: Flip a coin. If heads, your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Paralyzed.

d.flavorText: It can throw bubble-covered pebbles with precise control, hitting empty cans up to a hundred feet away.

d.name: Cramorant

attacks.name: Spit Shot
attacks.text: Discard all Energy from this Pokémon. This attack does 120 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon. (Don't apply Weakness and Resistance for Benched Pokémon.)

d.flavorText: It's an incredibly poor learner because it uses the bare minimum amount of energy for its brain. It focuses on battling instead.

d.name: Finizen

attacks.name: Aqua Slash
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't attack.

d.flavorText: Its water ring is made from seawater mixed with a sticky fluid that Finizen secretes from its blowhole.

d.name: Palafin

abilities.name: Zero to Hero
abilities.text: Once during your turn, when this Pokémon moves from the Active Spot to the Bench, you may search your deck for a Palafin ex and switch it with this Pokémon. Any attached cards, damage counters, Special Conditions, turns in play, and any other effects remain on the new Pokémon. If you switched a Pokémon in this way, put this card into your deck. Then, shuffle your deck.

d.flavorText: Its physical capabilities are no different than a Finizen's, but when its allies are in danger, it transforms and powers itself up.

d.name: Palafin ex
rules: Pokémon ex rule: When your Pokémon ex is Knocked Out, your opponent takes 2 Prize cards.

abilities.name: Hero's Spirit
abilities.text: Put this Pokémon into play only with the effect of Palafin's Zero to Hero Ability.

attacks.name: Giga Impact
attacks.text: During your next turn, this Pokémon can't attack.

d.name: Iron Bundle

attacks.name: Interjet
attacks.text: Switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon. If you do, switch out your opponent's Active Pokémon to the Bench. (Your opponent chooses the new Active Pokémon.)

d.flavorText: It resembles a mysterious object mentioned in an old book. There are only two reported sightings of this Pokémon.

d.name: Walking Wake

attacks.name: Aurora Gain
attacks.text: Heal 20 damage from this Pokémon.

attacks.name: Undulating Slice
attacks.text: Put up to 9 damage counters on this Pokémon. This attack does 20 damage for each damage counter you placed in this way.

d.flavorText: This ferocious creature is shrouded in mystery. It's named after an aquatic monster mentioned in an old expedition journal.

d.name: Wellspring Mask Ogerpon ex
rules: As long as this Pokémon is on your Bench, prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks (both yours and your opponent's).
